title: fighting jetlag by seeing theatre - the ashley hufford story ✈️🇬🇧#ash...
transcript: Is it insane to see two shows after taking a red eye flight from New York and landing at 7:00am in London? The answer is yes. But I'm on a West End theater trip and I was not going to waste a matinee slot. So on day one I got to my friend's flat by 9:30, took a little rest, got up, wash my face, and was ready for the day. The most important part was finding coffee, lots of coffee, before I headed over to meet my friends for pre show food. Ben was also coming off a red eye. Kate had just gotten there the day before, so we all were a little bit jet lagged, but caffeine is magic. So we got to the Trafalgar Theater feeling pretty great for the matinee of people, places and things. And I am so glad we powered through because I love this play so much. I was never even tired because I was so riveted. This is an intensely unnerving portrayal of addiction and rehab, and Denise Gough is giving one of the best performances I've ever seen. I really hope it comes to New York because I want to see it again. Afterwards I said goodbye to Ben and Kate because I was heading over to my second show of the day. Had a lovely little stroll down by the water as I was walking towards the tube, where I hopped on to head over to the Barbican Centre because I was Seeing Kiss Me Kate. I saw Kiss Me Kate on Broadway a few years ago and I honestly did not feel the need to see it again. Except that they went and cast Stephanie J. Block and then there was no way I could miss it. Because Stephanie J. Block is one of my favourite actresses and obviously she did not disappoint. She is an optional really Kate. Her voice, her acting, her humor. She has it all, really. Stamp is also in this production and he is just so delightful. Like, my only complaint is he's underutilized, but like, that role was underutilized. This production was extremely elaborate, directed by Bartlett Shere. Lots of crazy amazing choreography and big numbers. A perfect show to finish off day one.
